desc:
A binary min-heap is often stored in an array: the element at index i has its children at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2 (when they exist), and every element must be less than or equal to each of its children.

Given an array arr, return true if it is a valid min-heap in this layout and false otherwise.

[1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5]     -> true
[1, 3, 2, 2, 4]        -> false   (index 3 is a child of index 1: 2 < 3)
hints: Every element except the first has exactly one parent. Where is the parent of index i?
The parent of index i (i ≥ 1) is at index (i - 1) // 2.
It is enough to compare every element with its parent: arr[(i-1)//2] ≤ arr[i] for all i ≥ 1. Comparing with farther ancestors is implied by transitivity.
editorial: The heap property only talks about parent and child pairs. Because the relation ≤ is transitive, checking each parent against its direct children also guarantees that each element is at least as large as all of its ancestors.

Loop over i from 1 to n - 1 and compare arr[i] with arr[(i - 1) // 2]; return false at the first violation. This is O(n) time and O(1) space. No heap operations are needed: this is a check on the array, not a construction.
